payload.statement:
Chapter under review: ch14 (quarto-book/chapters/14-social-conflict.qmd), "Social Conflict", 134 lines.

Task: audit the chapter as a publishable unit and produce a disposition plan.
Each member audits through their own lens (see role card) and files a finding:
  stance support = the chapter holds on this lens as written
  stance refute  = the chapter must change; name the fix and its scope

Findings cite [file:line] in the chapter (14-social-conflict.qmd). Mechanics
findings state the broken value and the expected value. Cross-chapter checks
use the authoritative chapters as the reference, not this chapter (skill
roster = ch07, core rules = ch06, worked-example canon = ch01/ch03, GM rules
= ch19, reference tables = ch22).

Disposition classes (for the librarian's synthesis):
  mechanical    - safe to implement as a micro-PR (headings, tables, wording,
                  em-dashes, single-cell refs, budget rows)
  substantive   - needs a dispatched implementation pass (multi-file, new content)
  design-decision - needs Bruce's ruling; implement the recommended default,
                  flagged veto-revertible in decisions-pending.md

Standing book conventions are in force: zero em-dashes in book text; damage
budgets flat at Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21; card costs 2/4/8;
Adept prereqs exactly 2, Master exactly 3. Violations of these conventions
are findings, not questions.

payload.argument: As a publishable unit, chapter fourteen is structurally sound: an introduction that frames negotiation as the same dice engine spending a different currency, a four-entry primer on the social proficiencies, a four-row disposition table with mechanical effects, a five-step multi-round procedure, two guidance callouts, and a three-round worked example. The section order is logical, so no re-architecture is needed. However, it fails standing-convention and cross-reference checks, so the chapter must change before publication. I name the fixes and tier them for synthesis. Mechanical tier (safe single-file micro edits, each with a broken value and expected value): [14:29] the passive reading check is defined as the Knowledge score plus a flat 7, but the proficiency table in ch07 keys the same skill to the Reason attribute, and the worked example at [14:98] rolls Reason for the very same check; expected value is the book canon of the attribute score plus 7 as used in the surprise procedure and glossary, and [14:122, 14:131] invoke a bonus label, circumstance bonus, that appears nowhere in the core chapter or the reference sheet; expected value is rewording to the modifier categories the book actually uses. Substantive tier (dispatched implementation pass, multi-file): (a) the intimidation proficiency is taught here as a core social option, and the GM chapter's extended procedure lists it in its roll trio, yet it is absent from the skill roster in ch07, the reference table in ch22, and the glossary in ch21; the fix is either to add it to every roster (ch07, ch22, ch21, and any class favored-skill lists) or to excise it from this chapter and from ch19; (b) the extended-conflict procedure here (one roll per round, no opposition, each miss slides the NPC one step toward hostile, the side reaching three successes first prevails) diverges from the GM chapter's version (an opposed check, a tier table where a weak outcome hands a success to the other side, a strong outcome is worth two, a fumble hands two, a critical ends the scene at once, and stakes are fixed before play); the fix is to pick one canon and rewrite the other file to match. Design-decision tier (needs Bruce's ruling; implement the flagged default, veto-revertible in decisions-pending.md): (c) which attribute governs the passive reading number; recommended default keeps the existing book canon of the attribute score plus 7 and rewords line 29 to match; (d) which extended procedure is canonical; recommended default keeps this chapter's simpler loop because the chapter's own worked example follows it, and trims the GM chapter to a pointer plus the stakes rule. Convention sweep: zero em-dashes are present (only hyphen-minus, 53 of them), and no damage budgets, card costs, or prerequisite counts appear in this file, so the flat 2/4/6, 6/9/12, 9/15/21 budgets and the 2/4/8 card costs are not violated here. Cross-chapter probes for the other lenses: internal consistency (the attribute split at line 29 versus line 98, and the single-roll versus opposed framing at line 15 versus the extended section), cross-chapter agreement (ch07 roster, ch06 opposed-rolls and passive-Insight canon, ch19 procedure, ch22 tables), and editorial hygiene (heading hierarchy, table alignment, the two callouts, anchor labels, and the illustration placeholder).

payload.argument:
I re-audited ch14 (14-social-conflict.qmd, 134 lines) against the authoritative chapters. Verdict: the chapter must change. The arithmetic in the worked example is internally correct, but the chapter invents two named skills/mechanics that the book's own source-of-truth chapters do not define, and it contradicts ch19's extended-conflict rulebook on success counts and win conditions. Defects, broken -> expected:

1) PHANTOM SKILL (mechanical, single chapter): [14:27] the Social Skills section presents Intimidation (Brawn) as one of 'four skills' that drive social play. The roster in ch07 (source of truth) lists NO Intimidation row anywhere; its Social group is Persuasion (Guile), Insight (Reason), Deception (Guile), Performance (Guile). So the chapter's fourth social skill is a name that does not exist in the roster, and its Brawn attribute key has no roster entry either. Intimidation does appear in ch18 (retraining example) and ch19 (NPC quick-build) but never as a purchasable skill. Expected: either add Intimidation to the ch07 roster (substantive, book-wide) or drop it here and use a real roster skill; as written it is a phantom. Related: [14:21] says 'four skills' but the roster's actual four social skills differ (it omits Performance), so the framing is also off.

2) PHANTOM MECHANIC - 'circumstance bonus' (substantive): [14:122] and [14:131] grant 'a +1 circumstance bonus' for presence/intimidation. A whole-book grep finds the phrase 'circumstance bonus' NOWHERE else in the book. ch06's resolution system offers only Boon/Bane (4d6 keep best/worst 3) and named difficulty modifiers (Trivial +4 ... Nearly Impossible -6); there is no +1 'circumstance bonus' lever. Expected: replace with a real lever - a Boon (ch06: roll 4d6, keep the highest three) - or a named difficulty shift, since a flat +1 'circumstance bonus' is not a mechanic the engine supports.

3) WORKED-EXAMPLE BOON MISUSE (substantive): [14:104] Lyra's second roll is computed as 3d6 + Guile (+1) + 'Persuasion (no skill)' and the DA 'gives +1 for the Insight Boon', totaling 14 + 2 = 16 (Strong). The flat '+1 for the Boon' is not how ch06 defines a Boon: a Boon means roll 4d6 and keep the highest three, reshaping the curve ('worth roughly +2'), not a +1 flat modifier added to the total. Expected: a Boon is a 4d6-keep-3 reroll, not a +1; the stated modifier line and the +2 are mis-derived. (The 15+ Strong tier would still survive on Guile alone, but the arithmetic as printed is wrong.)

4) EXTENDED-CONFLICT RULES CONTRADICT CH19 (substantive, design-decision): The chapter's extended structure [14:56-58] is 'each round one PC rolls; first to 3 successes wins; failures shift attitude'. ch19's authoritative 'Social Conflict (Extended)' [19:187-196] says each round the roll is OPPOSED by the target's Insight/attribute, and its result table is: Weak = opponent gains 1, Standard = you gain 1, Strong = you gain 2, Critical = instant win, Fumble = opponent gains 2. Two hard contradictions: (a) success value - ch14 scores every success (including Strong) as exactly 1, but ch19 scores a Strong as 2 and a Critical as an immediate win; (b) win condition - ch14 wins at '3 successes' with no Critical instant-win, while ch19 has Critical = instant win. The chapter's worked example [14:106] also counts Lyra's Strong as only '1 success' where ch19 would award 2, so the example would actually end the conflict in round 2 under ch19. Expected: align ch14 to ch19's opposed-structure result table (Strong=2, Critical=instant win) or make ch14 explicitly the 'non-opposed' variant and reconcile the win math; as written the two chapters cannot both be right. This is a design-decision: pick one extended-conflict model.

5) PASSIVE INSIGHT - AGREE (support): [14:29] defines passive Insight as 'Knowledge score + 7'; ch13's surprise rule [13:197] also uses passive Insight = 'Knowledge score + 7'. The two agree, so this is clean. (Minor internal oddity, not a defect vs an authority: the active Insight skill keys to Reason in both ch07 and [14:29], yet the passive version keys to Knowledge - same skill, two attribute bases. Flag for the librarian, but ch13 matches the Knowledge+7 reading.)

6) WORKED-EXAMPLE CANON - AGREE (support): [14:86] Ser Aldric (Leader) rolls 3d6 + Guile (+1) + Persuasion Adept (+2), 4/5/3=12, +3 = 15 Strong - this matches ch03's Aldric canon exactly (ch03:136, same Guile +1 / Persuasion Adept +2, a different dice draw but same build and same 15/Strong). [14:98] Lyra's Insight roll (Reason +1, Insight Novice +1, 11+2=13 Standard) and [14:104] (14+2=16 Strong) are arithmetically self-consistent and use canon-consistent attribute values (Lyra Reason +1, Guile +1). So the example's dice math and character canon HOLD; the defects are the phantom skill, the phantom 'circumstance bonus', the Boon misuse, and the ch19 contradiction.

CONVENTIONS (support): zero em-dashes in the chapter (grep clean); no damage budgets, card costs, or prereq counts appear, so the standing numeric conventions are not implicated.

Disposition summary for the librarian: mechanical = fix the 'four skills' framing and the phantom Intimidation line if the roster is not being expanded; substantive = (a) reconcile or remove the 'circumstance bonus' (+1) against ch06, (b) fix the Boon misuse in the worked example, (c) reconcile the extended-conflict success/win math with ch19; design-decision = choose ONE extended-social-conflict model (ch14 non-opposed 3-successes vs ch19 opposed Strong=2/Critical-instant) so both chapters agree.

payload.argument: Stress-testing every rule in the chapter with concrete counter-examples. (1) Failure is undefined. Core tiers treat Weak as a success with a cost, Standard as a clean success, and only triple-1s as an outright miss [06:29-33,45]. Yet the Hostile row says a Standard result fails [14:39], so a player totaling 13 has both succeeded per the core engine and failed per this table; a DA must silently pick one. Fix: reword the row so only Strong moves a Hostile NPC while lesser totals hold or worsen the relationship (mechanical). (2) No Fumble row exists anywhere here. The extended loop folds triple-1s into ordinary misses that shift attitude one step [14:58], and the core fumble complications are all combat-themed [06:157-166]; a natural 1-1-1 before the king is mechanically identical to a plain 8. Fix: add Fumble and Critical rows to both the attitude and extended tables, aligned with the opposed table in the GM chapter [19:189-195] (mechanical). (3) The extended loop is one-sided. Each round exactly one PC rolls [14:56], the NPC never scores, and the first-to-three clause [14:57] can therefore only crown the party; since nearly every roll lands at Weak or above, three non-fumble results are near-certain and the conflict is a rubber stamp. The GM chapter instead runs opposed rolls where a Weak result gifts the opponent a point and a Fumble gifts two [19:187-197], so the two chapters give different games and the book never says which governs. Fix: port the opposed table into this chapter and state precedence (substantive). (4) Nothing ends a deadlock. Attitude drift is the only brake, and once Hostile is reached, continued misses only possibly conclude the talk [14:58] - DA whim, not a rule. A party that keeps producing Weak results can grind indefinitely under the fail-forward guidance [14:63-69]. Fix: hard bounds - three misses lose the conflict, or reaching Hostile ends it automatically (mechanical). (5) Attitude steps are one-directional. Downward movement is specified (one step per miss [14:58]), upward movement appears only in one table cell [14:39] and the example [14:88], and the fiction-driven insult rule [14:44] can fire in the same beat as a roll-driven step with no order of operations; insult an Allied NPC and both systems trigger at once. Fix: spell out both directions and forbid double shifts in one beat (mechanical). (6) The Allied freebie is unbounded and misapplied. 'Reasonable' is never scoped [14:42], and the example banks the winning third point on a roll-free grant while the warden is only Friendly [14:114] - a privilege the table reserves for Allied [14:42], since Friendly still requires rolls for favors [14:41]. Any demand can be framed as reasonable. Fix: scope reasonable (aligned interest, low cost, single request) and correct the example so the freebie comes only from an Allied NPC or a roll is inserted (substantive). (7) Passive Insight has no social comparison target. The formula appears [14:29], and the combat chapter pits it against Stealth [13:197], but nothing here states what a passive score is checked against when someone lies in conversation; a Deception 13 versus a guard with passive 7 is unresolved. Fix: state that an active Deception roll compares against the target's passive score as its threshold, or route active social contests through the opposed-roll rule [06:51-53] (mechanical). (8) The +1 circumstance bonus is invented, uncapped, and stackable. Core resolution offers exactly two levers - difficulty modifiers [06:178-185] and Boon/Bane, the former being 4d6 keep-highest-three worth roughly +2 [06:45-47]. A flat +1 for looming presence [14:122,131] appears nowhere else and stacks without cost, unlike the Aid maneuver which spends a combat Maneuver [13:57]; a five-hero party can pile +4 onto the speaker. Fix: replace with Boon or a difficulty-modifier bonus, capped at one contribution per roll (design-decision). (9) 'Insight Boon' misuses capitalized vocabulary. The example grants a flat +1 labeled Boon [14:104], but a Boon is a defined 4d6 curve change [06:45]; a player who read core rules will demand actual 4d6. Fix: grant a true Boon or lowercase the term (mechanical). (10) Difficulty label versus applied modifier. 'Standard difficulty' [14:84] does match the +0 label in the skills chapter [07:55], so the label is consistent; but the same line calls the cause sympathetic, the GM chapter urges rewarding favorable conditions with bonuses [19:41], and the example applies none without explanation. Fix: one sentence stating sympathy is already priced into Standard, or drop the word (mechanical). Net: the chapter must change; the one-sided race, absent Fumble/Critical handling, Friendly-yet-freebie example, and invented +1 are the sharpest failures.

payload.argument: Mechanics audit of ch14 (14-social-conflict.qmd), round 2. I re-verified every round-1 claim against the source lines myself and re-derived all roll math against ch06/ch07/ch19/ch22. Confirmed defects, each with broken value -> expected value: (1) Roll 4 arithmetic at 14-social-conflict.qmd:109: the printed equation "15 + 0 + 2 = 16" is false; the dice 6,5,4 sum to 15, Guile modifier is +0, the Adept Persuasion bonus is +2 per ch07:121, so the correct total is 17 (a Strong band total, same 15+ tier as the printed 16, but the printed sum is a 1-point error and the published equation misstates the addition). Rolls 1-3 recompute cleanly: 12+3=15 Strong; 12+2+0=14 Standard; 14+1+1=16 Strong. (2) Stale roster skill at line 114: Intimidation is named as a social skill, but the authoritative roster ch07:114-117 lists only Persuasion/Insight/Deception/Performance for the social group, ch22:168-171 omits it from the quick-reference, and the ch21 glossary has no entry; expected value: remove the row or add the skill to ch07+ch22+ch21 (a book-wide roster change). (3) Vocabulary error at line 104: the +1 die adjustment is labeled a "Boon", but Boon is defined in ch06:45 as a 4d6-keep-highest-three reroll with near-zero fumble odds; a flat modifier is not a Boon; expected value: relabel it a DA-granted modifier (the DA's discretion to grant +1 is supported by ch06:47's DA-guideline language). (4) Extended-conflict contradiction: the success-point mapping at lines 129-134 (Weak = 0 points, Standard = 1, Strong = 2, Critical = immediate win) and the one-roll-per-round structure at 125-126 conflict with the GM-guidance version at 19-gm-guidance.qmd:187-195, where Weak hands the opponent a success, every Standard-or-better scores one success, Strong scores two, Critical wins outright, and the first side to three successes takes the conflict; broken value = ch14's per-tier point table, expected value = ch19's table (ch19 is the designated GM-rules authority). (5) Rule completeness: ch14:129-134 gives no Fumble row, so a three-1s social roll in an extended conflict has no defined consequence beyond the generic ch06:153-166 complication table; ch19:195 handles it (opponent gains 2 successes). (6) Missing opposed mechanic: ch06:53 routes active social contests to this chapter, but ch14's single contested line (93) only restates the no-margin principle without a resolution procedure, leaving the "both sides actively contest" case undefined within the chapter. New checks that pass: zero em-dashes (counted U+2014 = 0); no damage-budget rows, so the flat 2/4/6-6/9/12-9/15/21 budgets are not violated; no card rows, so 2/4/8 costs and L3/L7 gates are untouched; the +1/+2/+3 tier bonuses and 2/4/8 DP costs at line 20-26 match ch07:120-124 exactly; the +4 to -6 difficulty table at 102 matches ch06:178-185; the 1-8/9-14/15-18+ bands match ch06:29-31; the passive Insight formula at line 29 (attribute + 7) matches ch13:197 and ch21:195, though "Knowledge score" is itself the legacy stat name (stale vocabulary, flagged as a secondary issue). The win condition is bounded (three points caps the conflict at line 127), so that specific completeness concern does not hold. Stance: refute; the chapter must be corrected (one arithmetic fix, one row removal, one relabel, one table alignment, one Fumble row) before publication.

payload.argument:
Full author audit of ch14 through the consistency/voice lens, with re-verification of the round-1 claims that touch voice or continuity.

VOICE: HOLDS. The opener [14:13] sits in the same register as ch13's [13:13] and ch06's [06:13] (punchy second-person, wry). The worked example [14:80-116] renders DA narration in italics exactly like ch01 [01:148] and ch13, and uses the house term 'DA' throughout (12 uses) with zero GM/DM drift. No em-dashes in the file (verified 0; layout-expert concurs). The flavor one-liners ('Works fast, burns bridges faster.'; the 'in social scenes, the safest result is that nothing happens' gag) are the book's signature voice and belong. No section is stat-block soup: two light tables and prose-forward guidance. No tonal drift, no cliche pile-up. On pure voice the chapter is publishable.

CONSISTENCY: FAILS on five points, so the chapter must change.
(1) PHANTOM SOCIAL SKILL (substantive, design-decision). [14:21] promises 'four skills' and [14:27] teaches Intimidation (Brawn) as one, but the authoritative roster ch07 Social group is Persuasion/Insight/Deception/Performance (ch07:136-139). Intimidation appears in no roster, and the chapter omits Performance, a real social skill. So the primer contradicts the book's own skill table and miscounts its own 'four'. Fix: rework the primer to the roster's four social skills (or add Intimidation to ch07/ch22/ch21 and drop Performance from the omission) - a Bruce ruling on whether Intimidation is a real skill.
(2) UNDEFINED BONUS LABEL (substantive). [14:122] and [14:131] grant 'a +1 circumstance bonus' for presence/intimidation. That label exists nowhere in the book; ch06's only levers are Boon/Bane (4d6 keep best/worst 3) and the named difficulty modifiers (ch06:172-178). A flat +1 'circumstance bonus' is an invented lever, and flavor is carrying hidden mechanics. Fix: reword to a real ch06 lever (a Boon, or a named difficulty shift) or define the label in ch06/ch22.
(3) PHANTOM NAMED BOON + WRONG MECHANIC (mechanical, corroborates round-1). [14:104] 'DA gives +1 for the Insight Boon' applies a Boon as a flat +1, but ch06:45 defines a Boon as rolling 4d6 and keeping the highest three; no named 'Insight Boon' exists in the book. Fix: apply a real Boon (4d6 keep 3) or a named difficulty shift, and stop inventing the name.
(4) PHANTOM CLASS/ROLE in the guidance (mechanical). [14:133] 'The ranger can mention a shared enemy' - Ranger is not a class in ch05 (nine core classes: Protector, Blade, Arcanist, Shepherd, Intellect, Odd, Leader, Unbalanced, Shadow) and not an ancestry in ch04; it appears only as a lowercase common noun (ch08:23). Fix: swap for a real class (e.g. the Shepherd/Animal link) or a generic 'a tracker'.
(5) WORKED-EXAMPLE SUCCESS COUNT vs OWN RULE (substantive, corroborates round-1). [14:57] says 'First to 3 successes wins' with each success worth one, but ch19's extended table awards Strong=2 and Critical=instant win (ch19:189-195), and the example's own [14:106] counts a Strong Persuasion as only 'Two successes'. The chapter's procedure and the GM chapter give two different games and the book never states which governs. Fix: port ch19's opposed table into ch14 (or state ch19 governs) and make the example's success math agree.

payload.argument: Final-quality audit of the social conflict chapter (134 lines). STRUCTURE: section order is sound - primer, disposition table, multi-round procedure, example, guidance - a reader who lands mid-chapter can follow. Two structural faults: (1) the two guidance blocks (the party-stacking rationale and the spotlight-distribution callout) sit after the worked example instead of beside the procedure they instruct, so a reader who opens at the procedure section misses them; (2) the chapter's intro promises the same 3d6 engine drives everything from haggling to treaties, yet the single-roll approach is never stated as an explicit procedure - only implied by the intro plus the disposition table, and invoked by name later as if already taught. CROSS-REFERENCES: verified by grep that the chapter contains zero @sec- pointers of its own, so nothing inside is broken; the inbound citation from the core chapter's opposed-rolls paragraph resolves to the chapter's heading label, so that link is clean. One structural omission: the GM chapter carries a parallel extended-conflict rulebook (opposed rolls, a five-row result table, a stakes-declared rule) and the two chapters never point at each other, so a reader at either location cannot discover the other rulebook exists. MISSING CONTENT (the load-bearing findings, all in the chapter's own table/procedure): (1) the extended loop says each round exactly one PC rolls and only failures move the NPC, yet the win clause speaks of the first side to three successes - as written the NPC side can never score, so the stated contest is a one-horse race and the clause is either dead wording or a missing opponent-scoring step (f-003 item 3 corroborated; mechanical-to-substantive: state opponent scoring or reword the clause); (2) the core engine's two dramatic extremes, triple-6s and triple-1s, have no rows here: the procedure folds them into ordinary outcomes, while the GM chapter's table awards an instant win and a two-point gift to the other side - the chapter must add Critical and Fumble rows or say why social play excludes them (f-003 item 2 corroborated; mechanical); (3) nothing bounds the conflict: at the worst disposition the text says further misses may end the talk, which is DA whim, not a rule; the GM chapter closes this hole with a stakes-declared requirement, this one has no equivalent, so a party producing middling results can grind indefinitely (f-003 item 4 corroborated; mechanical: add a hard end-state, e.g. three misses or reaching the worst disposition ends it); (4) the disposition table grants the no-roll-needed privilege only to the top attitude, but the worked example banks the winning third point on that exact privilege while the NPC stands one step below it - the example either needs the NPC at the top attitude or an inserted roll (f-003 item 6 corroborated; mechanical); (5) the example applies the core chapter's boon lever as a flat +1 added to the total, whereas the core chapter defines it as rolling four dice and keeping the highest three - a reader who learned the core rules will play it differently than the example shows (f-002 item 3 corroborated; mechanical reword or true 4d6). COMPLETENESS: single-roll encounters (implied), extended conflicts (present, gapped as above), failing forward (covered), worked example (present, one defect), DA guidance (present) - the chapter covers its topic end-to-end but ends with unresolved rule gaps inside the extended procedure rather than at the natural stopping point of the guidance callouts, and the placeholder illustration is still marked final-art-TBD, which is not publishable. EDITORIAL HYGIENE: no typos, no duplicated sentences, the game-master role term is consistent throughout (zero occurrences of the old GM term), the warden/guard/lieutenant names each stay consistent within their own context, no em-dash characters (53 hyphen-minuses, matching the zero-dash convention), and the double label (heading anchor plus the typst label block) is book-wide convention, not a chapter fault. RE-VERIFICATION OF ROUND-1 EDITORIAL CLAIMS: I independently confirmed the phantom-skill claim (the roster's social group has no intimidation entry, the reference sheet and glossary match the roster, so the chapter's fourth named skill is undefined in the book - f-001 and f-002 corroborated), the undefined bonus-category claim (a whole-book grep finds the phrase only in this chapter's two guidance lines - f-001 and f-002 corroborated), and the two-chapters-two-rulebooks claim (f-002 item 4 corroborated). The attribute-key split the librarian flagged (passive number keyed to one attribute while the active skill and the chapter's own example use another) I also confirm at the line level, but I classify it as a book-canonical design decision rather than an editorial fault, since the combat chapter and glossary match the chapter's formula; it belongs in the design-decision tier, not my broken/incomplete list. DISPOSITION: mechanical fixes - add Critical/Fumble rows to the extended procedure, add a hard conflict end-state, correct the example's no-roll-needed step, reword the boon application in the example, add a one-line pointer to the GM chapter's extended section (and ideally the reverse); substantive - decide and state opponent scoring or reword the win clause, state the single-roll approach as an explicit step list, move the two guidance blocks adjacent to the procedure; design-decision - pick one extended-conflict model (this chapter's loop versus the GM chapter's opposed table) and make the other chapter conform. On editorial-quality grounds the chapter is not publishable as written; stance refute.

Verification corrections first, for an honest audit trail: (1) f-001 (librarian r1) proposed rewording [14:29] passive Insight to Reason+7; this is REBUTTED on the ledger by f-005 (author) with line-level proof and confirmed by f-007 (EIC): ch13:197 (surprise rule) and ch21:195 (glossary) canon passive Insight as Knowledge score + 7, exactly matching [14:29], while active Insight rolls Reason (ch07:137) - line 29 STAYS, no fix. (2) f-004 (game-architect) item (1) claimed a printed equation '15 + 0 + 2 = 16' at line 109; FALSE - line 109 is Round-3 prose and the file contains only three rolls (lines 86, 98, 104), and line 104's '3, 6, 5 = 14 + 2 = 16' is internally correct (3+6+5=14; +Guile 1 +DA-granted 1 = 16); the real defect at 104 is only the label, a flat +1 called a 'Boon' although ch06:45 defines Boon as roll 4d6 keep highest three. f-004 item (4) cited a success-point table at lines 129-134; that table DOES NOT EXIST (lines 129-134 are the Face Problem callout) - ch14 has no per-tier point table; the ch14-vs-ch19 divergence is real but rests on ch14's procedure (lines 54-58: each success = one point, first to 3 wins, no Critical/Fumble rows, no opposed roll) versus ch19:187-196 (opposed rolls, explicit table Weak=opponent+1 / Standard=+1 / Strong=+2 / Critical=instant win / Fumble=opponent+2, stakes declared). (3) [14:39] Hostile row ('Standard fails, they dig in harder') is the attitude table doing its job - each attitude sets a higher bar, not a contradiction of the core tier definitions; no fix required (at most optional clarification wording). Consolidated defect set: SUBSTANTIVE - (a) phantom skill Intimidation (Brawn) at [14:27], absent from the ch07 roster (Social group = Persuasion/Insight/Deception/Performance), ch22, and ch21, yet referenced in ch18:94, ch19:83, ch19:187; fix direction ADD to every roster (22 to 23 skills), recommended default ADD (f-001, f-002, f-005). (b) extended-conflict rulebook split: ch14's non-opposed one-PC-rolls loop (lines 54-58; f-003 item 3, corroborated by f-007) vs ch19's opposed table; core ch06:53 (locked) routes 'social contests where both sides are actively working against each other' to the opposed-rolls rule and cites this chapter; recommended default: ch14 adopts the opposed model (ch19's table + stakes-declared rule), ch19 trims to a pointer, worked example re-derived (f-003, f-004, f-007). (c) worked-example defect cluster: [14:114] banks the winning third point on the Allied no-roll-needed privilege while the warden is only Friendly (line 88); [14:104] Boon mislabel; the example follows the loop that (b) changes, so it must be re-derived under the chosen model (f-002, f-004). MECHANICAL - (d) [14:133] 'The ranger' is not a class in ch05 (nine classes: Protector, Blade, Arcanist, Shepherd, Intellect, Odd, Leader, Unbalanced, Shadow); swap for a real class or 'a tracker' (f-005, f-007). (e) [14:122] and [14:131] '+1 circumstance bonus' is an invented lever appearing nowhere else; ch06's levers are difficulty modifiers and Boon/Bane; reword to a Boon (f-002, f-005). (f) no Critical/Fumble handling in the single-roll attitude path; add one line: triple 6s = automatic Strong with a flourish, triple 1s = automatic failure with a serious complication (f-003 item 2, f-007). (g) [14:29] defines passive Insight but never states what an active social contest compares against it; add one sentence that an active Deception roll is opposed by the target's passive Insight per ch06 (f-007). DESIGN-DECISION (implement recommended default, log veto-revertible in decisions-pending.md): (1) Intimidation roster entry; (2) opposed-vs-non-opposed extended model; (3) circumstance-bonus replacement (Boon default). Explicitly NOT defects, recorded to stop re-flagging: passive Insight = Knowledge+7 at [14:29] (canon per ch13:197, ch21:195); the Hostile row bar at [14:39] (attitude table's purpose); zero em-dashes (verified); illustration placeholder (book-wide convention); double-label typst block (book-wide convention); Ser Aldric/Lyra canon (matches ch03:134-142, ch01:146); roll math at lines 86/98/104 (arithmetically correct as printed). The sole support, f-006 (layout-expert), verified against the built PDF pages 224-231: zero em-dashes, tables clean, figure/caption pattern and double-label block are book-wide conventions - no ch14-specific layout defect.
